purpose: F-01 next-work item from VERIFIER_NEXT_EVIDENCE.md: 'reduce SDK code'. Breaks down exactly where the 183,090-byte actual Soroban SDK contract wrapper (over the 131,072-byte code cap) differs from the 127,068-byte raw verifier module (which fits), to find whether a quick, low-risk fix (Cargo profile flags, avoidable soroban-sdk features) closes the gap. Finds no such quick fix exists; the gap is inherent soroban-sdk contract-ABI glue.
method: A new, dependency-free Python script (no wasm-objdump/twiggy/wasm-opt available in this environment) parses the WASM binary module format directly and sums per-section byte sizes, run against the two already-built, already-pinned artifacts: the raw verifier module (fits the code cap) and the actual compact Soroban SDK contract wrapper (exceeds it). Read-only against existing build artifacts; builds nothing new, deploys nothing.

delta.note: code and data account for 56,021 of the 56,022-byte delta; export/import/function/global/type/element/datacount changes are noise-level (under 300 bytes combined, with export actually 147 bytes smaller in the SDK build).

ruled_out_as_quick_fixes.candidate: Cargo release profile flags (opt-level, lto, codegen-units, panic, strip)
ruled_out_as_quick_fixes.finding: Both the raw-module build and the SDK-wrapper build already use the same aggressive settings: opt-level 's' or 'z', lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic='abort', strip='symbols'. There is no unapplied flag to try.
ruled_out_as_quick_fixes.source: tools/binius-verifier-next (raw) vs tools/binius-soroban-research/compact/Cargo.toml (SDK wrapper), both read directly.

ruled_out_as_quick_fixes.finding: soroban-sdk 25.3.2 defines no [features] default set at all (features: alloc, docs, experimental_spec_shaking_v2, hazmat, hazmat-address, hazmat-crypto, testutils; none implied by default). The contract's dependency line already enables only 'alloc', which the verifier's heap-based field arithmetic requires. There is nothing further to disable.

conclusion: The 56,022-byte gap is not a tuning oversight; it is the inherent cost of soroban-sdk's contract entry-point glue (host-function import bindings, Env/Val/XDR marshaling, the guest allocator, and the three required custom metadata sections: contractspecv0, contractmetav0, contractenvmetav0, totalling 544 bytes and not a meaningful contributor on their own). Closing this gap further would require either hand-rolling the Soroban contract ABI without soroban-sdk's abstractions (a substantial, higher-risk re-engineering effort, not attempted here) or waiting on upstream soroban-sdk size improvements. This is independent of, and smaller in magnitude than, the CPU-instruction budget gap (canonical verification exhausts the full 400M-instruction budget; see verifier-profile-research.json for where that cost concentrates), so closing code size alone would not by itself make this backend deployable.
profiler_availability_note: A real sampling/instruction-level profiler (perf, valgrind/callgrind) would be needed to decompose the CPU-cost side (the 94-97% 'Layer B' step identified in verifier-profile-research.json) any further than tracing-span granularity allows. Neither is installed in this environment; apt has candidates for both (linux-tools-generic, valgrind) but installing them requires sudo, which is not available non-interactively here. Not pursued without the user's explicit go-ahead to install system packages.
scope_and_limits: Static section-size accounting only; does not measure runtime CPU cost (see verifier-profile-research.json for that).
Read-only against existing, already-built artifacts; no new build, deployment, or account/asset action taken.
Does not itself reduce code size or close F-01; it rules out the cheapest category of fix and identifies the actual source of the overhead.
